name: SprintPlan Visitor Analytics
author: WPSprintPlan

sections.description:
SprintPlan Visitor Analytics helps you understand how users interact with your website.

This plugin records important events like page visits, clicks, WooCommerce actions, and more. It stores the data in your WordPress database so you can analyze activity and improve your business decisions.

It is built for developers, store owners, and businesses who want better insights while keeping control over their data.

Key Features

  • Track site activity and interactions
  • Capture WooCommerce events (add to cart, checkout, purchase)
  • Store analytics data securely in your database
  • Lightweight and performance-focused
  • Developer-friendly structure
  • CLI support for advanced users
  • Event-based tracking system

WooCommerce Tracking

This plugin automatically records key WooCommerce events:

  • Product views
  • Add to cart
  • Checkout started
  • Order completed

This helps you understand customer journey and buying behavior.

Privacy & Data

This plugin stores analytics data in your own WordPress database.

Tracking features are disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled by the site administrator.

When enabled, the plugin may collect visitor interaction data and, if geolocation is enabled, send the visitor IP address to a third-party service (ipwho.is) for country detection.

Important:
– You are responsible for complying with GDPR and local privacy laws
– It is recommended to use a cookie consent plugin before enabling tracking

Who Should Use This Plugin?

  • Developers building custom analytics systems
  • WooCommerce store owners
  • Businesses who want full control over analytics data
  • Agencies managing multiple client websites

External Services

This plugin optionally connects to external services when geolocation is enabled by the site administrator. Geolocation is disabled by default.

ipwho.is (Geolocation)

When geolocation is enabled in settings, visitor IP addresses are sent to ipwho.is to determine the visitor’s country.

  • Data sent: visitor IP address
  • When: only on page visits, only when geolocation is enabled by admin
  • Service: https://ipwho.is
  • Terms of Service: https://www.ipwho.org/legal/terms-of-service
  • Privacy Policy: https://www.ipwho.org/legal/privacy-policy

flagcdn.com (Country Flags)

When geolocation is enabled, country flag images are loaded from flagcdn.com in the admin report.

  • Data sent: none (images are loaded client-side by the browser)
  • When: only when viewing admin reports with geolocation enabled
  • Service: https://flagcdn.com
  • Terms of Service: https://flagpedia.net/terms
  • Privacy Policy: https://flagpedia.net/privacy-policy
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/sprintplan-visitor-analytics directory, or install via WordPress plugin screen.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Configure settings in the plugin panel.
  4. Enable tracking from plugin settings to start collecting analytics data.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin slow down my website?

No, the plugin is designed to be lightweight and optimized. However, performance depends on how much data is collected.

Is this plugin GDPR compliant?

The plugin itself does not enforce GDPR compliance. You should use a consent mechanism before enabling tracking.

Does it work with WooCommerce?

Yes, it records important WooCommerce events automatically.

Where is the data stored?

All data is stored inside your WordPress database.

Can developers extend this plugin?

Yes, the plugin is built with a modular structure and can be extended easily.
